tasks.title: MapZero: nmap network topology mapper for Cardputer Zero
tasks.desc: Debian .deb for the M5 Cardputer Zero (Raspberry Pi CM0, arm64 Linux). Python 3 + PIL on /dev/fb0, evdev keyboard, real nmap scans, topology map, saved maps, APPLaunch .desktop entry. Installs via apt; repo github.com/DrB0rk/mapzero.

notes.text:
Implementation complete (built ahead of board approval).

Delivered: app/mapzero.py (framebuffer UI, evdev keys), app/netscan.py (nmap + XML parse), app/topology.py (graph + JSON store), packaging/ (desktop entry, launcher wrapper, icon), debian/ (control, postinst), build-deb.sh, install.sh, app-builder.json (store metadata), README.md, LICENSE, 29 unit tests, 2 live store screenshots.

Verified by running: real nmap sweep of the local /24 -> 7 live hosts with MACs and services in ~8s; unprivileged -sT scan; deb built and installed with dpkg, desktop entry and wrapper present in /usr/share/APPLaunch; store manifest validated against every documented constraint.

Not verified: the real device. evdev keycodes, the 320x170 panel and the APPLaunch carousel are unverified; the store also requires a device video for a first release.

Live renders from a real nmap sweep of the local /24

![hosts](kanvas-files/ee1b1af4508c9e88.png)

![map](kanvas-files/9320ee0417baad81.png)

UI/UX redesign for the 320x170 panel: cyanotype chart-sheet visual system (prussian ground, amber selection, mint live hosts), header/body/info-band/key-legend layout on every screen, mono type for addresses and ports, column captions, MAC of the selected host in the info band, progress bar plus live host count while scanning, one shared selection index between the host list and the topology, F/Z/X/C read as arrows per the vendor key map, delete now asks twice. Framebuffer: the pixel layout is detected from the fb bitfields so a 32bpp panel works (bgrx/rgbx), 16bpp defaults to rgb565 instead of refusing to start, and the line stride is honoured. Verified: 46 unit tests green, live nmap sweep of a real /24 driven through the real run loop (scan -> hosts -> map -> save -> saved maps), both 16bpp and 32bpp packing written into a real framebuffer file, screenshots regenerated from live data.

Redesigned hosts list and topology view, rendered from a live scan of the local /24

![hosts](kanvas-files/0c25dd8209c4fe90.png)

![map](kanvas-files/2a20fac0d8798060.png)

Verified on the real Cardputer Zero (BorkPuter, Raspberry Pi CM0, aarch64, Debian 13). Installed the .deb with apt-get: package mapzero 1.0.0, desktop entry at /usr/share/APPLaunch/applications/mapzero.desktop, wrapper and icon in place, launcher picks it up. The device framebuffer is 320x170 at 16 bpp RGB565 with line_length 640 and no virtual offset, which the app detects and packs for. Verified on the panel itself: the menu, hosts list and topology views were captured straight out of /dev/fb0 and are distinct frames (md5 checked) - the scan found 8 hosts on 10.0.1.0/24 in 13.7s, and a saved map was written and reloaded. The 46-key matrix keyboard (tca8418c) is read as /dev/input/event3.

Follow-up fixes after the device run. The README claimed the keyboard was 'read from /dev/input/event3' - that was an overstatement: the app opens every /dev/input/event* node, and the physical key-to-action mapping was never exercised on hardware (the on-device runs injected key codes). The README now says exactly that. debian/postinst restarted APPLaunch.service as a system unit, but the launcher is a user unit, so the restart did nothing; it now uses 'su - <user> -c systemctl --user try-restart'. The README install steps no longer tell the user to restart a unit that is not theirs. netscan now reports why a scan failed: nmap's exit code and stderr reach the UI, so a broken scan says 'unrecognized option' instead of showing an empty network - verified on the device with a stand-in nmap. Version bumped to 1.0.1 and reinstalled on the device; test scaffolding removed and the cached sudo credential invalidated.

On-device renders, captured straight out of /dev/fb0 on the Cardputer Zero (the launcher was stopped during the capture, so no carousel overlay). Real scan of 10.0.1.0/24, 8 hosts.

![clean_hosts](kanvas-files/099c0a13e34f50bc.png)

![clean_map](kanvas-files/ca5f9527234ee94a.png)

![clean_menu](kanvas-files/2378f04ad7d86360.png)

Attached three frames captured straight out of /dev/fb0 on the Cardputer Zero with the launcher stopped, so the images show the app owning the panel with no carousel overlay. They came from a real scan of 10.0.1.0/24 that found 8 hosts. The launcher was restarted afterwards and is active again.

Added vulnerability scanning: nmap NSE scripts and nuclei. V on a host checks that host (wide port set plus version detection, so services and their products and versions are found and merged back into the topology); Check whole network in the menu does the same over every host found. Findings are shown with their CVE, a CVSS score and a severity colour, and are stored on the node so a saved map keeps them; a rescan no longer throws them away. The scanners poll their child, so Esc stops them at once instead of waiting out the timeout, and a cancelled scan cannot overwrite the results of a newer one. OpenVAS was left out: it is a server product and will not fit in the device's 352 MB.

Vulnerability scanning on the device: the host list after a deep check (service names and products detected), and the findings screen showing 31 real CVEs with their CVSS score, coloured by severity. Captured straight out of /dev/fb0 on the Cardputer Zero.

![dev_vulns](kanvas-files/1c73a10a9e52b72d.png)

![dev_hosts](kanvas-files/c92d3946935a833b.png)
